summary: Kimi CLI is installed on the VPS as "Kimi Code" v0.43.1 at C:\Users\Administrator\.kimi-code\bin\kimi.exe (151 MB standalone binary, mtime 2026-09-15 08:53). It is NOT on PATH and NOT installed via npm/pip/pipx — it is a self-contained per-user install with an auto-updater. Authentication is a device-code OAuth flow (not an API key): credentials at C:\Users\Administrator\.kimi-code\credentials\kimi-code.json (mtime 2026-09-15 11:25) hold Bearer access_token/refresh_token, scope=kimi-code, and the provider "managed:kimi-code" points at https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1 with source=oauth — i.e. the Kimi Code coding-subscription endpoint, consistent with the OWNER's USD 99/month subscription and distinct from a platform pay-as-you-go API balance. Region is mainland-cn (kimi.com). A single live headless call (kimi -p "Reply with exactly the word OK." --output-format text) succeeded: exit 0, 6.2 s latency, returned "OK" — auth works. Headless mode is -p/--prompt with --output-format {text,stream-json}, model selection via -m (4 models: kimi-for-coding/K2.8 1M ctx default, k3 1M, highspeed & k3-256k at 256K), permission modes --auto (never ask) and -y/--yolo. There is NO usage/quota/account/limits subcommand — spend cannot be queried programmatically via the CLI. No existing QuantMechanica Kimi wrapper exists in the repo and no KIMI_ flags exist under D:/QM. An ACP-over-stdio server mode (kimi acp) exists and is the most robust programmatic integration path.

risks: Text output mode (--output-format text) mixes a version banner, thinking bullets, and a session-resume trailer around the answer, so naive stdout capture will NOT yield a clean response — an adapter must use stream-json or strip the wrapper lines.

No usage/quota/limits subcommand: the USD 99 subscription's remaining allowance cannot be checked via the CLI. Spend/rate must be tracked externally (or scraped from the status_line JSON snapshot). This is a real blind spot for governance/pacing analogous to quota_governor.

Access token lifetime is only 900s (15 min); relies on the refresh_token for continuity. If the refresh flow fails (region block, revoked device), headless calls will fail and require an interactive `kimi login` device-code flow — not automatable headlessly except via `kimi acp --login`.

Auto-update is enabled (auto_install=true) and the binary self-updates on a staged rollout; an adapter pinned to CLI flag/output behavior of 0.43.1 could break silently after an upgrade. Consider pinning or monitoring version.

Region is mainland-cn (api.kimi.com). If the VPS network path to kimi.com is throttled/blocked (this VPS is documented as bot-blocked on YouTube), latency/availability of Kimi calls could degrade; not verified beyond the single 6.2s call.

No documented CLI timeout flag — a hung/long generation must be bounded by an external watchdog; the interactive TUI launches if arguments are malformed (subcommand help via wrong argv dropped into the TUI during this audit), which in a headless context would hang until externally killed.

stream-json output format and whether -p reads a prompt from stdin (vs only the argument) were NOT live-verified (audit was limited to one live call); recommendations relying on them are documented-but-untested and should be confirmed before production use.
unknowns: Documented failure/exit codes: only exit 0 (success) observed. kimi --help does not enumerate non-zero exit codes; error-class -> exit-code mapping is UNKNOWN and must be characterized empirically before building robust error handling.

Whether `kimi -p` reads the prompt from stdin when the argument is omitted (enabling large/piped prompts) — UNKNOWN; only the -p <arg> form was documented and tested. Large prompts via argv may hit the ~32KB Windows command-line limit; no --prompt-file flag is documented.
Exact structure of --output-format stream-json events (message/thinking/usage framing) — UNKNOWN; not live-tested (one-call limit). Needs one probe run to design the parser.
Concurrency / rate-limit behavior and whether parallel headless invocations are allowed under the subscription — UNKNOWN; not documented locally and not tested.
Remaining subscription quota / monthly allowance and reset date — UNKNOWN and not queryable via CLI (see risks).
Whether the status_line JSON 'usage' field contains subscription-level remaining quota vs per-session token counts — UNKNOWN (would require configuring a status_line command, out of read-only scope).

Global diagnostic log rotation policy and whether transcripts contain full prompt/response content usable for audit — partially seen (session index lines only); user-history jsonl content not inspected in depth.

integration_points.what: kimi.exe -p "<PROMPT>" --output-format stream-json -m kimi-code/kimi-for-coding --auto  (run with cwd set to the target dir, or add --add-dir <dir>). Use full path C:\Users\Administrator\.kimi-code\bin\kimi.exe since it is not on PATH.
integration_points.why: -p is the documented non-interactive one-shot; --auto prevents any interactive permission prompt from hanging a headless run; -m pins the model; stream-json avoids the banner/thinking/resume-trailer contamination seen in text mode. Evidence: kimi --help; live text-mode output showed the contamination.

integration_points.what: Prefer parsing stream-json events (confirm event schema with one probe first). If forced to use --output-format text, strip: leading line matching '^kimi version ', any lines beginning with the thinking bullet '• ', and the trailing 'To resume this session: kimi -r ...' line; the residual is the answer.
integration_points.why: Live call in text mode returned exactly those wrapper segments around 'OK'. Evidence: first-600-char capture of the live call.

integration_points.what: Wrap every invocation in an external timeout (e.g. Start-Job/Wait-Job or a subprocess timeout of 120-300s); kill on expiry. Do not rely on a CLI timeout flag (none exists).
integration_points.why: No documented timeout option; trivial call took 6.2s but generations can run long; malformed argv can launch the TUI and hang. Evidence: kimi --help has no timeout flag; subcommand-help misfire launched the TUI during audit.

integration_points.what: Treat exit 0 = success. On non-zero exit or empty answer, classify as (a) auth-expired -> requires `kimi acp --login` / interactive `kimi login` device-code re-auth (cannot be done silently), (b) transient network/region error -> retry with backoff, (c) other -> surface. Verify auth health cheaply via `kimi provider list` (prints source=oauth) and config via `kimi doctor` before a batch.
integration_points.why: Auth is OAuth with a 900s access token auto-refreshed by refresh_token; provider list and doctor are non-LLM health checks. Exit-code taxonomy is otherwise undocumented (UNKNOWN). Evidence: provider list, doctor outputs; credentials fields.

integration_points.what: For anything beyond one-shot prompts, drive `kimi acp` (Agent Client Protocol server over stdio) rather than repeated -p spawns; use `kimi session list --json` to enumerate/resume sessions and `kimi export -o <zip>` to archive transcripts for the evidence trail.
integration_points.why: ACP is the documented stdio server mode; session list --json and export give scriptable session/evidence management. Evidence: kimi acp --help, session list --help, export --help.

integration_points.what: Do NOT expect a CLI usage query. Track Kimi invocations/tokens in an external ledger (mirror the quota_governor pattern) or, if needed, configure a tui.toml status_line command to capture the JSON 'usage' snapshot. Budget against the USD 99/month subscription, not a per-call API balance.
integration_points.why: No usage/quota subcommand exists; usage is only exposed to a status_line command's stdin JSON. Evidence: kimi --help command list; tui.toml status_line comment.

integration_points.what: Record the CLI version per run (banner/`--version`) and be aware auto_install=true will self-update the binary; re-validate adapter flags/output after version changes.
integration_points.why: tui.toml [upgrade] auto_install=true with an active staged rollout manifest. Evidence: tui.toml, updates/latest.json, rollout.log.
